stanzas.sanskrit:
दक्षो विरिञ्चितनयोऽथ मनोस्तनूजां
लब्ध्वा प्रसूतिमिह षोडश चाप कन्याः ।
धर्मे त्रयोदश ददौ पितृषु स्वधां च
स्वाहां हविर्भुजि सतीं गिरिशे त्वदंशे ॥ १६-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Prasuti , another daughter of Swayambhu Manu, was married to the son of Brahma, Daksha Prajapathi and they had 16 daughters. Out of these 16, thirteen were married to Dharma Deva. Swadhaa was married to Pitrus; Swaaha to Agni and Sati was married to Shiva.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
dakṣo viriñcitanayo’tha manostanūjāṃ
labdhvā prasūtimiha ṣoḍaśa cāpa kanyāḥ |
dharme trayodaśa dadau pitṛṣu svadhāṃ ca
svāhāṃ havirbhuji satīṃ giriśe tvadaṃśe || 16-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
मूर्तिर्हि धर्मगृहिणी सुषुवे भवन्तं
नारायणं नरसखं महितानुभावम् ।
यज्जन्मनि प्रमुदिताः कृततूर्यघोषाः
पुष्पोत्करान् प्रववृषुर्नुनुवुः सुरौघाः ॥ १६-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Out of the thirteen married to Dharma Deva, one was Murthi who gave birth to the divine twins - NARA and NARAYANA, who were the forms of Bhagwan. They were always together. The Gods in the heavens rejoiced at this birth, singing and showering heaps of flowers.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
mūrtirhi dharmagṛhiṇī suṣuve bhavantaṃ
nārāyaṇaṃ narasakhaṃ mahitānubhāvam |
yajjanmani pramuditāḥ kṛtatūryaghoṣāḥ
puṣpotkarān pravavṛṣurnunuvuḥ suraughāḥ || 16-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
दैत्यं सहस्रकवचं कवचैः परीतं
साहस्रवत्सरतपः समराभिलव्यैः ।
पर्यायनिर्मिततपः समरौ भवन्तौ
शिष्टैककङ्कटममुं न्यहतां सलीलम् ॥ १६-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
The asura Sahasra Kavacha, was protected by a thousand coats of armor. No one could break them without performing thousand years of penance and at the same time fighting with him simultaneously for the same thousand years.
Bhagwan as Narayana with Nara did the required in turns and destroyed all the coats of the Asura but one remained. Then Bhagwan killed him effortlessly, as a sport.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
daityaṃ sahasrakavacaṃ kavacaiḥ parītaṃ
sāhasravatsaratapaḥ samarābhilavyaiḥ |
paryāyanirmitatapaḥ samarau bhavantau
śiṣṭaikakaṅkaṭamamuṃ nyahatāṃ salīlam || 16-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अन्वाचरन्नुपदिशन्नपि मोक्षधर्मं
त्वं भ्रातृमान् बदरिकाश्रममध्यवात्सीः ।
शक्रोऽथ ते शमतपोबलनिस्सहात्मा
दिव्याङ्गनापरिवृतं प्रजिघाय मारम् ॥ १६-४ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Nara and Narayana went to Badarika Ashrama to settle down for teaching and practicing the path to "MOKSHA". Indra could not stand this and wanted to see their spiritual downfall and so sent celestial women to distract them.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
anvācarannupadiśannapi mokṣadharmaṃ
tvaṃ bhrātṛmān badarikāśramamadhyavātsīḥ |
śakro’tha te śamatapobalanissahātmā
divyāṅganāparivṛtaṃ prajighāya māram || 16-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
कामो वसन्तमलयानिलबन्धुशाली
कान्ताकटाक्षविशिखैर्विकसद्विलासैः ।
विध्यन्मुहुर्मुहुरकम्पमुदीक्ष्य च त्वां
भीतस्त्वयाथ जगदे मृदुहासभाजा ॥ १६-५ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Kaamadeva accompanied by spring season and the Malaya breeze, tried to attack Bhagwan many times by the arrows with glances and their amorous movements. Finding Bhagwan unaffected, they were frightened.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kāmo vasantamalayānilabandhuśālī
kāntākaṭākṣaviśikhairvikasadvilāsaiḥ |
vidhyanmuhurmuhurakampamudīkṣya ca tvāṃ
bhītastvayātha jagade mṛduhāsabhājā || 16-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
भीत्यालमङ्गज वसन्त सुराङ्गना वो
मन्मानसं त्विह जुषुध्वमिति ब्रुवाणः ।
त्वं विस्मयेन परितः स्तुवतामथैषां
प्रादर्शयः स्वपरिचारककातराक्षीः ॥ १६-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Bhagwan addressed Kaamdeva, Spring and damsels and asked them not to fear and revealed to them the beautiful handmaids attending on Bhagwan.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
bhītyālamaṅgaja vasanta surāṅganā vo
manmānasaṃ tviha juṣudhvamiti bruvāṇaḥ |
tvaṃ vismayena paritaḥ stuvatāmathaiṣāṃ
prādarśayaḥ svaparicārakakātarākṣīḥ || 16-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
सम्मोहनाय मिलिता मदनादयस्ते
त्वद्दासिकापरिमलैः किल मोहमापुः ।
दत्तां त्वया च जगृहुस्त्रपयैव सर्व-
-स्वर्वासिगर्वशमनीं पुनरुर्वशीं ताम् ॥ १६-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Kaamadeva and others who had come to overpower Bhagwan, were themselves captivated by Bhagwan’s handmaids' fragrance. They accepted Urvasi’s beauty which put to shame the beauty of all the celestial damsels.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
sammohanāya militā madanādayaste
tvaddāsikāparimalaiḥ kila mohamāpuḥ |
dattāṃ tvayā ca jagṛhustrapayaiva sarva-
-svarvāsigarvaśamanīṃ punarurvaśīṃ tām || 16-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वोर्वशीं तव कथां च निशम्य शक्रः
पर्याकुलोऽजनि भवन्महिमावमर्शात् ।
एवं प्रशान्तरमणीयतरावतारा-
-त्त्वत्तोऽधिको वरद कृष्णतनुस्त्वमेव ॥ १६-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Seeing all this, Indra was perplexed, and thus realized Bhagwan’s glory. This incarnation of Bhagwan as Nara Narayana which is so gentle and beautiful, is excelled only by Bhagwan’s incarnation as Krishna.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
dṛṣṭvorvaśīṃ tava kathāṃ ca niśamya śakraḥ
paryākulo’jani bhavanmahimāvamarśāt |
evaṃ praśāntaramaṇīyatarāvatārā-
-ttvatto’dhiko varada kṛṣṇatanustvameva || 16-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
दक्षस्तु धातुरतिलालनया रजोऽन्धो
नात्यादृतस्त्वयि च कष्टमशान्तिरासीत् ।
येन व्यरुन्ध स भवत्तनुमेव शर्वं
यज्ञे च वैरपिशुने स्वसुतां व्यमानीत् ॥ १६-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Daksha was arrogant due to his dominating rajo guna, lost his mental calmness and developed hatred for Lord Shiva. He further went to the extent of insulting his own daughter Sati.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
dakṣastu dhāturatilālanayā rajo’ndho
nātyādṛtastvayi ca kaṣṭamaśāntirāsīt |
yena vyarundha sa bhavattanumeva śarvaṃ
yajñe ca vairapiśune svasutāṃ vyamānīt || 16-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
क्रुद्धे शमर्दितमखः स तु कृत्तशीर्षो
देवप्रसादितहरादथ लब्धजीवः ।
त्वत्पूरितक्रतुवरः पुनराप शान्तिं
स त्वं प्रशान्तिकर पाहि मरुत्पुरेश ॥ १६-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
Lord Shiva, angry at the insult of his wife, destroyed Daksha's sacrifice & cut off his head. Lord Shiva restored Daksha's life again after being requested by other Gods &  Daksha attained mental peace also.
Bhattathiri requested Lord Guruvayoorappa who brings peace to devotee's heart to free him from ailments.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kruddhe śamarditamakhaḥ sa tu kṛttaśīrṣo
devaprasāditaharādatha labdhajīvaḥ |
tvatpūritakratuvaraḥ punarāpa śāntiṃ
sa tvaṃ praśāntikara pāhi marutpureśa || 16-10 ||
